source_attestations.note: Approval-ready verification; rules sections 5–8 re-checked against Oracle, rulings and CR

summary:
Mishra lets you counter your own artifact spells and still get them. The list's stax pieces (Void Mirror, Vexing Bauble, Chalice, Nether Void, Nullstone Gargoyle, Blood Funnel, Planar Chaos, Possibility Storm) counter or tuck your artifacts, and Mishra's trigger, ordered below, puts them onto the battlefield. It closes with Top loops, KCI recursion, Karn + Lattice and Lattice + Vandalblast. Twenty Spellbook lines are confirmed; representative ones are cited.

Rules surprises: in singleton Mishra finds only the spell itself; a Chalice Mishra returns comes in at X=0; Possibility Storm stops overloaded Vandalblast. Flags: your stax hits your own instants and sorceries; Void Mirror and Bauble cut off your own loops when Mishra is gone.

interactions.title: In singleton, Mishra only finds the spell itself after it's countered or moved
interactions.ruling: Mishra triggers when you cast an artifact spell. It looks for a card with the same name in your graveyard, hand or library. The list is singleton, so the only such card is the spell itself, and while it's on the stack Mishra finds nothing. The trigger pays off only when another trigger you control moves the spell first, by countering it into the graveyard or tucking it into the library. Put Mishra's trigger on the stack first and the counter or exile trigger on top, so that one resolves first. The trigger doesn't need the spell to resolve.
interactions.short: Singleton: Mishra hits only once your own trigger counters or tucks the spell; order Mishra below it.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast an artifact spell, you may search your graveyard, hand, and/or library for a card with the same name as that spell and put it onto the battlefield. If you search your library this way, shuffle.

source.quote: His trigger does not require that artifact spell to resolve.
the controller may order the relevant triggers so the counter effect resolves first and Mishra's trigger resolves afterward.

interactions.title: Self-counters as parity breakers: Blood Funnel, Nether Void, Nullstone Gargoyle, Chalice, Void Mirror, Vexing Bauble, Planar Chaos
interactions.ruling:
Each of these can counter your own artifact spell before Mishra's trigger resolves, and then Mishra puts the card onto the battlefield from your graveyard:
- **Blood Funnel:** decline the sacrifice. The artifact still got its {2} discount.
- **Nether Void:** decline the {3}.
- **Nullstone Gargoyle:** your first noncreature spell of the turn.
- **Chalice:** mana value equal to its counters.
- **Void Mirror:** no colored mana spent.
- **Vexing Bauble:** no mana spent.
- **Planar Chaos:** a lost coin flip.

A countered artifact ends up on the battlefield anyway. Opponents have no Mishra, so their spells just stay countered.
interactions.short: Own counter trigger above Mishra's → artifact countered into graveyard → Mishra puts it onto the battlefield.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, counter that spell unless you sacrifice a creature.
Whenever a player casts a spell, if no colored mana was spent to cast it, counter that spell.
Whenever a player casts a spell, if no mana was spent to cast it, counter that spell.

rulings.quote: Players may cast spells that they know Vexing Bauble will counter. Any abilities that trigger when spells are cast will still trigger and resolve if appropriate, and any effects that count how many spells are cast will still count those spells if appropriate.

source.quote: a noncreature artifact spell can be countered when its controller declines/fails the sacrifice

interactions.title: Possibility Storm + Void Mirror / Vexing Bauble lock; Mishra recovers the tucked artifact
interactions.ruling:
Every spell cast from hand is exiled, and its caster may cast a random card of the same type for free. Void Mirror or Vexing Bauble then counters that free spell, because no mana was spent on it. That shuts off spells cast from hand for everyone.

You can still use Mishra. When you cast an artifact from hand, put Possibility Storm's trigger above Mishra's. Storm puts the original on the bottom of your library, then Mishra searches your library and puts it onto the battlefield. If the free replacement is also an artifact, it triggers Mishra too, and when it gets countered into the graveyard Mishra can recover it.

It's not a total lock. Spells cast from other zones (Mystic Forge, Bolas's Citadel, Emry) and spells where mana was spent on additional costs get through.
interactions.short: Storm + Mirror/Bauble counters all hand-cast spells; Mishra still lands your artifacts.

oracle.quote: Whenever a player casts a spell from their hand, that player exiles it, then exiles cards from the top of their library until they exile a card that shares a card type with it. That player may cast that card without paying its mana cost. Then they put all cards exiled with this enchantment on the bottom of their library in a random order.

rulings.quote: The original spell is part of the group of exiled cards put on the bottom of the library in a random order. If the exiled card that shared a card type with that card wasn't cast, it's also part of this group.

spellbook.quote: If the player chooses to cast the spell, Void Mirror triggers, countering that spell since no colored mana was spent to cast it.
If the player chooses to cast the spell, Vexing Bauble triggers, countering that spell since no colored mana was spent to cast it.

source.quote: Mishra's original trigger resolves afterward and can find the original named artifact card now in the library and put it directly onto the battlefield.

interactions.title: Your own stax hits your non-artifact spells, and Possibility Storm breaks overloaded Vandalblast
interactions.ruling:
Mishra rescues only artifacts. Your instants and sorceries (Force of Will, Mana Drain, Demonic Tutor, Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift, Swan Song) face your own taxes:
- **Blood Funnel:** sacrifice a creature or the spell is countered.
- **Nether Void:** pay {3} or it's countered.
- **Nullstone Gargoyle:** your first noncreature spell each turn is countered.
- **Planar Chaos:** each spell has a 50% chance to be countered.
- **Possibility Storm:** each spell from hand becomes a random one of the same type.

Overloaded Vandalblast is half of the Mycosynth Lattice line. With Possibility Storm out, Vandalblast from hand gets exiled, and a free sorcery can't be cast for its overload cost. Have these pieces off the table, or Mishra plus enough mana ready, before you cast key non-artifact spells.

flag.note: Blood Funnel, Nether Void, Nullstone Gargoyle, Planar Chaos and Possibility Storm counter or replace your own instants and sorceries (Mishra saves only artifacts), and Possibility Storm stops the Lattice + overloaded Vandalblast kill.

oracle.quote: Whenever a player casts a spell, counter it unless that player pays {3}.
Whenever the first noncreature spell of a turn is cast, counter that spell.

rulings.quote: If you cast a spell without paying its mana cost, you can't choose to cast it for any alternative costs, such as overload costs. You can pay additional costs, such as kicker costs. If the spell has any mandatory additional costs, you must pay those.

source.quote: Additional costs paid with mana, uncounterable effects, trigger interaction, and spells not cast from hand can change the outcome.

interactions.title: Without Mishra, Void Mirror and Vexing Bauble break your own Top and KCI loops
interactions.ruling: Your Top loops cast Sensei's Divining Top for {0} (Forge or Reality Chip plus a {1} reducer) or for 1 life (Citadel). No mana is spent, so Vexing Bauble and Void Mirror counter it. KCI recasts paid only with colorless mana get hit by Void Mirror too. With Mishra out, each countered Top or loop piece goes from the graveyard to the battlefield. Mishra's trigger is ordered below the counter, so the loop keeps going, and cast triggers (Aetherflux, Jhoira, Uthros) still count each cast. Without Mishra, the loop stops at the first counter.

flag.note: With Void Mirror or Vexing Bauble out, the Top/Forge/Citadel/Reality Chip and KCI loops only continue while Mishra is on the battlefield.

oracle.quote: {T}: Draw a card, then put this artifact on top of its owner's library.
If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost.

rulings.quote: If a spell is cast with an alternative cost that includes mana (such as flashback), Vexing Bauble's first ability won't trigger and won't counter that spell. Similarly, if a spell is cast without paying its mana cost, but the player did pay mana for additional costs such as from kicker or from Thorn of Amethyst, Vexing Bauble's first ability won't trigger and won't counter that spell.

spellbook.quote: Cast Sensei's Divining Top from the top of your library by paying {0}.
Cast Sensei's Divining Top from the top of your library by paying 1 life.

interactions.title: Chalice of the Void returned by Mishra has X = 0
interactions.ruling: If Mishra puts a countered Chalice onto the battlefield from your graveyard, it wasn't cast, so X is 0 and it enters with no charge counters. A Chalice on 0 counters every mana value 0 spell, including your own Moxen (Chrome, Diamond, Opal, Amber) and Lotus-style rocks. Mishra's search is optional, so decline it unless you want Chalice on 0.

oracle.quote: This artifact enters with X charge counters on it.

rulings.quote: If there are zero charge counters on Chalice of the Void, it counters each spell with a mana value of 0. This includes face-down creature spells cast with morph's alternative cost.

interactions.title: Karn + Mycosynth Lattice lock; Lattice + overloaded Vandalblast
interactions.ruling: Lattice makes every permanent an artifact, so Karn's static stops opponents from activating any ability of their permanents, including land mana abilities. Your own permanents aren't affected. Overloaded Vandalblast with Lattice out destroys every permanent you don't control. Lattice doesn't make spells artifacts, so it doesn't add Mishra triggers. Encroaching Mycosynth does: your nonland permanent spells and cards become artifacts, so creature spells trigger Mishra too. Karn's −2 for a card from outside the game isn't relied on.
interactions.short: Karn + Lattice = opponents can't activate anything; Lattice + overload Vandalblast = one-sided wipe.

oracle.quote: Activated abilities of artifacts your opponents control can't be activated.
All permanents are artifacts in addition to their other types.

rulings.quote: Mycosynth Lattice turns all permanents on the battlefield into artifacts. Spells on the stack and cards in other zones aren’t permanents, so those spells and cards don’t become artifacts.

Encroaching Mycosynth turns all permanents you control into artifacts. Permanent spells you control become artifact spells in addition to their other types, and nonland permanent cards you own in other zones become artifact cards in addition to their other types.

spellbook.quote: Mycosynth Lattice turns all permanents into artifacts.
Cast Vandalblast for its overload cost, paying {5} to destroy all permanents opponents control.

source.quote: Karn prevents opponents from activating abilities of artifacts, including mana abilities of their lands.

interactions.title: Top loops: Forge or Reality Chip + {1} reducer; Citadel + Aetherflux
interactions.ruling: Tap Top to draw and put it on top of your library. Then cast it again from the library: with Mystic Forge, or Reality Chip attached to a creature, and a {1} reducer, it costs {0}. With Bolas's Citadel it costs 1 life, and Aetherflux Reservoir gains more each cast. The recast Top is a new untapped object. Each cast also triggers Jhoira, and Uthros at 3+. See mishraap-05 for Void Mirror and Vexing Bauble.

oracle.quote: As long as The Reality Chip is attached to a creature, you may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library.
You may cast artifact spells and colorless spells from the top of your library.

spellbook.quote: Activate Sensei's Divining Top by tapping it, causing you to draw a card and put Sensei's Divining Top on top of your library.
Aetherflux Reservoir triggers, gaining you 1 life for each spell you have cast this turn.

source.quote: Mystic Forge + Sensei's Divining Top + an artifact cost reducer + Aetherflux Reservoir.

interactions.title: KCI + Scrap Trawler + Myr Retriever (+ reducer / Junk Diver + Sol Ring); Emry + The One Ring
interactions.ruling:
Sacrifice Myr Retriever to KCI. It returns Scrap Trawler to your hand, and Trawler returns the lower-mana-value piece when it dies, so the pieces cycle through your hand. Recasting them is mana-neutral with one {1} reducer. The Junk Diver + Sol Ring version makes infinite colorless mana with no reducer. Each recast is an artifact spell, so Aetherflux, Jhoira and Uthros trigger.

With Emry, sacrifice The One Ring to KCI and recast it from your graveyard each turn. Ring's protection needs it to be cast, so the Emry line gives protection from everything every turn.

oracle.quote: Whenever this creature dies or another artifact you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, return to your hand target artifact card in your graveyard with lesser mana value.
When The One Ring enters, if you cast it, you gain protection from everything until your next turn.

spellbook.quote: When Myr Retriever dies, it triggers, returning Scrap Trawler from your graveyard to your hand.
Activate Emry by tapping it, allowing you to cast The One Ring from your graveyard this turn.

source.quote: Krark-Clan Ironworks + Scrap Trawler + Myr Retriever / Junk Diver recursion structures

interactions.title: Uthros Research Craft: Mishra stations 4; draw resolves first, even if the artifact is countered
interactions.ruling: Station by tapping Mishra (power 4, sorcery speed). That's 4 charge counters, past the 3+ threshold in one go. After that, every artifact spell you cast draws a card. The draw resolves before the spell, so it still happens when your own Void Mirror or Bauble counters it on the way to Mishra.

oracle.quote: 3+ | Whenever you cast an artifact spell, draw a card. Put a charge counter on this Spacecraft.

rulings.quote: The triggered ability granted by Uthros Research Craft’s second ability resolves before the spell that caused it to trigger. It resolves even if that spell is countered or otherwise leaves the stack without resolving.

source.quote: The draw trigger is independent of whether the artifact spell later resolves or is countered.
